topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the opening framing and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Genetic and environmental determinants of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how intrinsic biological processes, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures interact to determine cancer susceptibility and population patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens and viral infections contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated through the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how radiation and metabolic activation of chemical compounds induce direct and indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, tissue proliferation, and host developmental stages facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methods for assessing carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogens and assess human risk.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the closing summary and final concluding remarks for the lecture.
